newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps ease in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps ease in late trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Thursday, dealers said.
They said operators were also seen unloading swaps in the afternoon after the central bank raised its fixing.
The rupiah weakened slightly at midday after rumours of riots in Jakarta which turned out to be an early morning territorial dispute between two gangs near a Jakarta textile trading centre.
Spot rupiah eased to 2,363.75 briefly and bounced back later as offshore players received confirmed reports.
One U.S. bank dealer said response was brief and less drastic than reports over banks liquidation on Wednesday.
Dealers said operators seemed to focus on other issue after clarification from central bank governor that it was some rural and not commercial banks which were in liquidation process.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,362.90/63.10 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,362.50/63.50. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,361.3/61.5 and 2,360.5/61.0, respectively.
One Japanese bank dealer said swap premiums came under some pressure following anticipation of central bank dollar buying on Thursday after a higher fixing on Thursday afternoon.
He said players hoped liquidity would be ample next week and this may put swap rates under renewed pressure.
Overnight swap was at 0.5/0.6 and tom/next at 1.5/1.6.
One-month swap was at 12.75/13.15, two at 24.0/24.5, three at 37.00/37.90 and six at 76.0/77.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,363/2,555 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,363/2,411 on Thursday.
